text:
marta: seeing a recurrent p99 blip on canary-3 over the last 12h, looks tied to a small fraction of requests that: long prompt + tool-call -> reentrant gen. p95 stable, p99 jumps ~6x. attaching quick flame sample and a short log.
jon: can you dump the profiler snippet? curious if kernel switch is happening mid-request or if batching is causing head-of-line blocking.
sasha: fwiw we saw something similar last month but with cache eviction thrash. did you check KV hit rates for those sessions?
marta: attaching logs:
```
[2026-03-17T21:04:12Z] req=abc123 prompt_len=820 tool_calls=2 kv_hits=0 kernel=fast_gemm -> slow_fallback
[2026-03-17T21:04:13Z] reentry: triggered toolcall callback -> queued for inference
[2026-03-17T21:04:18Z] p99=4500ms p95=320ms
```
darryl: kv_hits=0 is suspicious. long prompts should warm prefix cache. are these new sessions or resumed sessions? maybe client sends a different session id.
kevin: also check microbatch sizing. if a long prompt holds a slot and we allow batch growth to N=32 it can inflate latency for co-batched short queries. what's current microbatch cap?
marta: microbatch max currently 24 on canary. short bursts coalesce so the long request ends up waiting on a batch completion. profiler shows kernel fallback at token 512 -> switch to slow_f16 path.
jon: two levers: reduce max microbatch for latency SLO (<8) or add a per-request fastpath that forces immediate dispatch for long-context/high-toolcall flags. tradeoff is throughput cost.
sasha: another option: aggressive KV prefetch for long prompts. if we prewarm KV for session on first few tokens we can avoid the cold eviction -> kernel fallback path.
kevin: small experiment idea: set microbatch_max=8 on a 10% canary, keep throughput measurement. if p99 drops with acceptable qps loss, we can roll. Also try sticky kernel pins for models that touch tool-calls often.
marta: agreed. I'll spin a canary with microbatch_max=8 + kv_prefetch=true and collect p95/p99 and tokens/sec. schedule: start at 00:30 UTC for 1 hour.
ops-bot: Canary job started (canary-3) with overrides: {microbatch_max:8, kv_prefetch:true} at 2161234600
jon: nice. if that helps, consider a heuristic: if request has >1 toolcall OR prompt_len>700 -> immediate dispatch (bypass batching) + small batch cap.
sasha: low-risk patch: add metric for kernel_switch_count per-request and alert when >0 for >0.1% of requests. that will help catch regressions earlier.
marta: thanks all. i'll post the canary results here after the run. :thumbsup:
kevin: :raised_hands:
